evidence_class: mocked: an in-process caller and a SQLite catalog file stand in for the collector, the network and the central database; no HTTP server, Pod or hive collector runs
interfaces: hooks.memory.api.ingest.ingest(catalog, grant, request) is the POST /v2/sessions/ingest contract as a function: it checks schema major version 2, the envelope and every event's sequence, byte range and project before authorization, rejects the whole batch with forbidden_scope when the corpus or any event project is outside the Grant, and returns a response only after Catalog.commit returns

hooks.memory.api.ingest.event_identity(session_uid, source_generation, event) is the sha256 of the session, source generation, sequence and byte range, so any worker or connection derives the same event_id for the same source event

hooks.memory.catalog.Catalog(path).commit(batch) runs one BEGIN IMMEDIATE SQLite transaction in WAL mode with synchronous FULL: a known batch_id with the same payload digest returns its stored result as replayed with the current watermark, a different digest is a revision_conflict; otherwise events are inserted once per sequence, an identical event is counted as a duplicate, a different event at a committed sequence is a revision_conflict that rolls the batch back, unsupported records are quarantined with sequence and reason, and the batch result and the contiguous durable watermark are written in the same transaction

hooks.memory.catalog.Catalog.duplicate_events_total(access_domain) reads the durable ingest_duplicate_events_total counter, incremented in the committing transaction by each duplicate event and by every event of a replayed batch

supported_versions.schema_version: 2.x; any other major version is invalid_request
supported_versions.records: SV2-SES-01 TranscriptRecord kinds as the SV2-SES-02 collector and SV2-SES-03 spool carry them
supported_versions.storage: SQLite with WAL journal and synchronous FULL on a local or mounted disk

states.observed: Cases A, B and C each ran twice from independent temporary catalogs with identical records.
states.accepted: A batch is accepted when its envelope, events and grant pass; an accepted batch can still be refused as a revision_conflict inside the transaction.
states.committed: A response with state committed or replayed is returned only after the SQLite commit; durable_through is the highest contiguous sequence committed or quarantined for the session and source generation.
states.externally_verified: None: no central database server, network transport or deployed collector was exercised.

metrics.ingest_duplicate_events_total: Catalog.duplicate_events_total(access_domain), durable in the catalog per access domain

atomicity_rule: One event outside the grant, a malformed event envelope or a conflicting event rejects the whole batch and changes nothing; an authorized event whose record is not a supported normalized record is quarantined with its sequence and reason while the rest of the batch commits.

rollback_rehearsal.action: Stop calling ingest from any producer; the catalog file keeps committed events, quarantine rows, batch results and watermarks, and a later retry of any batch replays its committed result.
rollback_rehearsal.authoritative_objects: session_event, session_quarantine, session_ingest_batch and session_watermark rows; none is a cache and none is deleted by rollback.
rollback_rehearsal.proof: Case C loses the response after commit, opens a new catalog on the same file, finds the three committed events, retries the batch and receives the committed watermark as replayed with no second copy, then a later stale retry of the same batch returns the newer watermark without lowering it.

remaining_limitations: No HTTP server exposes POST /v2/sessions/ingest yet; callers use the function directly.
The SV2-SES-03 spool flusher is still not wired to ingest: a spool Entry carries records without the session, generation and byte ranges that ingest requires.
The catalog is SQLite; the Postgres session schema of the plan and its migration framework are not implemented.
Grants are passed in by the caller; no principal is authenticated here.
compatibility: Explicitly local compatibility path: ingest accepts the SV2-SES-01 TranscriptRecord kinds unchanged and stores each record exactly as submitted; the collector, spool, whole-file reader and memory store are untouched.
authority: The corpus and every event project come from the caller's Grant; a project label inside a record is never read as permission, and an unattributed event stays unattributed.
